query: Any US federal agency announcements in August 2026 about evaluating frontier AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic for national security, cybersecurity, or biosecurity risks? Include CAISI, NIST, DOE, DoD, CDAO, NSA, DHS, and any pre-deployment testing agreements.
answer:
Report submitted. Summary of what I found:

**No qualifying event has occurred in the elapsed portion of the window (Aug 10–19, 2026).** The last announcement that would have fit the criteria was CAISI's on **May 5, 2026** — well before the window.

Three findings matter most for how this question resolves:

1. **The active August channel is deliberately non-public.** EO 14409 (signed June 2, 2026) routes frontier-model review through Treasury/NSA/CISA with an explicitly *classified* benchmark and *nondisclosure* requirements written into §3(b)(ii). The White House has said outright it won't release the framework. The Aug 1 deadline passed with zero public deliverables, and the Aug 4 industry meeting was deliberately staff-level — reporting noted executives weren't expected because it "is not being staged as a public rollout."

2. **The closest thing to a window event is not an agency announcement.** WIRED's Aug 12 *Inner Loop* piece reports the framework currently covers only closed models from Anthropic and OpenAI, and that pressure inside the administration "could even result in leading AI labs working as formal partners in testing programs." But it is entirely anonymously sourced and names no federal agency at all.

3. **The DoD path is structurally blocked for a *joint* announcement.** Anthropic was designated a national security supply chain risk in Feb 2026 and excluded from the 8-company classified-networks agreement in May 2026, while OpenAI signed its own separate deal. I found no evidence that rupture has been resolved.

Two things cut the other way and are worth flagging: attendees at the Aug 4 meeting floated "a future event related to the proposal," and **Aug 29 is the two-year anniversary of the original AISI–OpenAI/Anthropic MOUs**, falling inside the window.

Base rate for announcements naming both companies is roughly one per 8 months (Aug 2024, Sept 2025, May 2026). 15 of the 24 window days remain.

One caveat I want to be explicit about: because the framework is designed not to be announced, an agreement could in principle be concluded without ever becoming public. That is a genuine limit on what any amount of searching can establish here.

sources.title: Controlling Advanced Artificial Intelligence: Executive Order 14409 Explained (CRS)
sources.snippet: July 9, 2026 — The order calls for a classified benchmarking process to determine whether an AI system qualifies as a covered frontier model (to be defined within 60 days, August 1, 2026) based on its cyber capabilities. Companies are asked to participate in a voluntary review process giving the government a 30-day window.

key_facts: NO qualifying announcement found as of Aug 19, 2026: no US federal agency has officially announced new or materially expanded voluntary agreements to evaluate frontier models from BOTH OpenAI and Anthropic after Aug 10, 2026.

The most recent qualifying-type event was May 5, 2026, when CAISI (NIST/Commerce) announced new frontier AI national security testing agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft and xAI, and simultaneously noted that OpenAI and Anthropic had RENEGOTIATED their existing partnerships to align with America's AI Action Plan. This is before the question window.

Executive Order 14409, 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security,' was signed June 2, 2026. Section 3 set a 60-day deadline (Aug 1, 2026) for Treasury, the Secretary of War through the Director of NSA, and DHS through the Director of CISA to design a voluntary frontier model review framework, in consultation with the National Cyber Director, APST, and Commerce through NIST.

CRITICAL STRUCTURAL FACT: EO 14409 Section 3(b)(ii) grants government access to covered frontier models 'subject to appropriate confidentiality, cybersecurity, insider-risk, and intellectual-property protection, use, and nondisclosure requirements.' The EO contains NO provision requiring public announcement of agreements with AI developers.

Both the classified benchmarking methodology and the threshold determining which models qualify as 'covered frontier models' are CLASSIFIED under EO 14409, shared with developers and researchers only 'as appropriate.' The NSA Director makes the designation determination.
On Aug 1, 2026 the EO deadline passed with no public deliverables: no Federal Register notices, no NIST or CISA publications, and no OSTP statements were issued, per contemporaneous reporting.

On Aug 4, 2026 the White House Office of the National Cyber Director hosted a STAFF-LEVEL meeting (executives explicitly not expected; reporting stated it was 'not being staged as a public rollout') with Meta, Nvidia, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and smaller companies to review the completed framework.

The White House stated it has NO PLANS to publicly release the framework. A White House official said: 'Just because things are unclassified that doesn't mean we are going to broadcast them to everyone.' Fortune headlined the decision 'baffling.'
Attendees at the Aug 4 meeting floated the idea of 'a future event related to the proposal, perhaps to continue discussing it' — no date or format was specified.

The single most window-relevant item is WIRED's Inner Loop report of Aug 12, 2026 (Hugo Lowell), which states the framework currently applies ONLY to closed models from Anthropic and OpenAI, is expected to expand to open models 'in the coming months,' and that the White House is under pressure from other parts of the administration to draw up 'a more robust arrangement with leading AI labs' that 'could even result in leading AI labs working as formal partners in testing programs.'

The WIRED Aug 12 report is entirely anonymously sourced ('people familiar with the matter,' 'a White House official tells Inner Loop,' 'sources suggest') with no named official, no agency spokesperson, and no on-the-record statement. No government agency is named anywhere in the piece. It does NOT constitute an official agency announcement.

A weekly AI regulation and policy review published Aug 17, 2026 covering 18 sources does not mention CAISI at all, does not mention EO 14409, and connects no federal agency (DOE, DoD, NSA, DHS) to OpenAI or Anthropic in any evaluation capacity.

DoD context is strongly negative for a joint announcement: in Feb 2026 Trump said the government would not work with Anthropic and Anthropic was designated a national security supply chain risk; on May 1, 2026 DoD expanded classified AI work with 8 companies (SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Reflection, Microsoft, AWS, Oracle), explicitly EXCLUDING Anthropic. No evidence of resolution located as of Aug 19, 2026.
OpenAI signed its own separate Department of War classified-network agreement (announced Feb 27, 2026, updated March 2, 2026) — an asymmetric, single-company arrangement.

Base rate: US federal announcements naming BOTH OpenAI and Anthropic for model evaluation occurred approximately 3 times in 24 months — Aug 29 2024 (AISI MOUs), Sept 2025 (CAISI works with OpenAI and Anthropic), and May 5 2026 (renegotiated partnerships) — roughly one per 8 months.
The original AISI-OpenAI/Anthropic MOUs were announced Aug 29, 2024, making Aug 29, 2026 a two-year anniversary that falls inside the question window.

As of May 5, 2026 CAISI had completed more than 40 evaluations, including of state-of-the-art models that remain unreleased; agreements support testing in classified environments, and developers frequently provide CAISI with models that have reduced or removed safeguards. Interagency feedback flows through the CAISI-convened TRAINS Taskforce.

The most recent CAISI news item located is 'CAISI Assessment of Z.ai's GLM-5.2' (July 2026), an assessment of a PRC open-weight model — not a US lab agreement. NIST's CAISI feed shows no July or August 2026 agreement announcements.

DOE/NNSA work with the two labs is real but asymmetric and predates the window: Anthropic-NNSA nuclear risk classifier (Sept 2025), OpenAI-DOE collaboration, and the DOE 1,000 Scientist AI Jam (2025). No Aug 2026 DOE announcement located.
Axios reported Aug 4, 2026 that the Trump AI framework excludes open AI models; the framework's current scope debate concerns ADDING open models rather than expanding OpenAI/Anthropic commitments.
